root_cause.text: In the DRM/msm DPU runtime suspend path, `dpu_runtime_suspend()` incorrectly called `dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0)`, which dropped the power/voltage performance vote while the core clock was still configured for the maximum rate, leaving voltage and frequency mismatched on resume.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0)` from `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/disp/dpu1/dpu_kms.c::dpu_runtime_suspend()`, and the CVE text states this call “drops the MMCX rail to MIN_SVS while the core clock frequency remains at its original (highest) rate,” causing the rail to be unable to sustain the clock rate after runtime resume.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the OPP rate reset from runtime suspend so the device no longer drops its performance vote at that point.
intent_record.what: Two lines were removed from dpu_runtime_suspend(): the comment "Drop the performance state vote" and the call to dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0) before clk_bulk_disable_unprepare().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the suspend path no longer explicitly drops the device's OPP/performance-state vote during runtime suspend; it now only disables and unprepares the clocks and continues with the remaining suspend logic.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the OPP rate reset from runtime suspend so the device no longer drops its performance vote at that point.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the erroneous dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0) call from runtime suspend, preventing the premature drop of the voltage/performance vote while the clock remains at max rate.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct faulty call that drops the OPP performance vote during runtime suspend, causing the voltage/frequency mismatch described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call clears the OPP performance vote during runtime suspend. Per the root cause, doing so while the core clock remains configured for the maximum rate leaves voltage and frequency mismatched on resume.

In `dpu_runtime_suspend()` the code explicitly says `/* Drop the performance state vote */` and then calls `dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0);` before disabling clocks. This matches the root cause: dropping the OPP/performance vote during suspend while the core clock is still configured can leave voltage/frequency mismatched on resume. There is no compensating handling here (no preservation of the current rate or setting the OPP to the active clock rate), so the fix is not present in this snippet.
